doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: One week with Ella Fitzgerald and the borrowed bass
summary: He misses connecting with Ella's group by leaving his bass in a baggage room, then borrows a bass against his ring and plays a week with her.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: I think I lost about, at that time I lost about ten or fifteen pounds. Of course today that would be great. But anyway that went on for a while and then I says I have to do something about this. I says it’s time for me to make a change. Because I’ve heard other people talking about that they needed a trade, and they were tired of going from one gig to the other and so on. But during this time in Boston, I got one good gig, I think I had a week with Ella. She was coming through Boston, or was in Boston already and they needed a bass player for Philadelphia. So I went down to the station with my bass. I was supposed to meet them. And I looked around and I didn’t see anybody, no Ella, no anybody. You know I’m just a kid, nobody. And so I says well maybe I should just hop on the train and I’ll see them at the next station or somewhere. So what I did, I don’t know why I did this, but I put my bass in the baggage room and left it there and I stayed on the train and sure enough there they were, waiting at the platform looking for me. “I wonder where the kid is.” There was Marcus Foss, the drummer who called me Junior, that type of thing. And Don Abney who was the piano player, and all these guys were well seasoned. And so Ella says, “oh there he is,” she says, “where’s your bass honey?” I said it’s at the station and then I tried to explain it and I couldn’t explain it. So that upset her quite a bit. And she says, “honey, always keep your bass with you.” She says, “Ray always took his bass with him wherever he went.” Because she used to be married to Ray. And so we hopped on the train to go to Philly. But my mentor, Dean, told me he says, “always keep a diamond on your finger, so whenever you have a problem you’ll be able to eat anyway.”

So I had a little diamond ring that I had bought, because I was following my mentor see? Which was excellent advice. So I went to the music store and they had an old bass in the corner and I says, “well look man,” I said, “I’m working down here at Pep’s, and all I have is my ring, can I use your bass for a couple of days?” So he looked at the ring, he

says, “yeah, okay.” So he loaned me this bass, he asked me who was I working with. I told him Ella Fitzgerald, that type of thing, and so I took the bass and went down and worked with her a few days. Then in the meantime we sent for my other bass. And so it arrived, my Chubby Jackson model. And so I took it back. That’s how that happened, one week with Ella.
Yeah I bet the bass from the pawn shop didn’t have five strings on it.
Well actually no. It didn’t. Actually it wasn’t a pawn shop, it was a music store.
All the musicians used to go in there. As a matter of fact I bought my Ray Brown method book from there. Sure.
